userdoc.notice: Creates a launch and buys for its recipient in one transaction.

factory().notice: Launch factory this contract creates tokens through.

launchAndBuy((string,string,string,strin.notice: Launches a token and immediately buys `quoteIn` of its curve for `recipient`, both in this transaction.

devdoc.title: Atomic Clank launch and initial buy

SafeERC20FailedOperation(address).details: An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.

Launched(address,address,address,address.details: quoteSpent is the requested quoteIn, including any refunded portion, as in Pons.

devdoc.details: Adapted from the MIT-licensed PonsV2LaunchAndBuy. The cited upstream deployment is an exact Sourcify match: chain 4663, 0xe33E9E479dF8802cb0866d5d05258bEc4cF62948. The factory trusts this router to preserve the caller's deployer identity.

params.params: Launch parameters, forwarded to the factory untouched. Set `creatorFeeRecipient` explicitly; Clank does not pay creator fees. Set `expectedEconomics` to the value `previewLaunchEconomics` returned, which still pins the terms as it would on a direct launch.
params.quoteIn: Amount of the quote asset to spend on the opening buy. An amount past what the curve can sell is clamped by the curve and the remainder comes back to the caller.
params.pairToken: Quote asset, or the zero address for a native launch.
params.minTokensOut: Slippage bound on the opening buy. The curve prices a clamped fill against this too, so a buy sized to take the whole allocation can still set a meaningful floor.
params.launchConfigId: Factory launch config to launch against.
params.snipeTaxExemptions: Additional recipients to exempt from the launch-window snipe tax. `recipient` is appended automatically. At most 31 entries may be supplied because the factory caps the combined list at 32.

launchAndBuy((string,string,string,strin.details: For a native launch the call must carry the launch fee and the buy together. For an ERC-20 quote asset it carries the launch fee only, and the buy is pulled from the caller, who must have approved this contract for `quoteIn` first.
